audits.title: Quality of pathology reports for advanced ovarian cancer: are we missing essential information? An audit of 479 pathology reports from the EORTC-GCG 55971/NCIC-CTG OV13 neoadjuvant trial.
audits.standard: Quality indicators: macroscopic description, measuring and weighing, tumour origin and differentiation

cycle1.result: All specimens described in 92.3%; major samples measured and weighed in 59.9%; tumour origin missing in 20.5% (primary) and 23.4% (interval debulking).

audits.other_findings: Differentiation missing in 10% and 20.8%; quality differed by country; synoptic reports recommended.
audits.citation: Verleye L, Ottevanger PB, Kristensen GB, Ehlen T, Johnson N, van der Burg ME, et al.. Quality of pathology reports for advanced ovarian cancer: are we missing essential information? An audit of 479 pathology reports from the EORTC-GCG 55971/NCIC-CTG OV13 neoadjuvant trial. Eur J Cancer. 2011;47(1):57-64. doi:10.1016/j.ejca.2010.08.008. PMID: 20850296.

audits.title: An Audit of 204 Histopathology Reports Over Three Years of Carcinoma of Cervix: Experience from a Tertiary Referral Centre.
audits.standard: Minimum data set for carcinoma cervix histopathology reports
audits.setting: Tata Memorial Hospital, tertiary referral centre, Mumbai

cycle1.result: Minimum dataset compliance generally good; pTNM stage not mentioned in 65.06%; mean pelvic lymph node yield 16.6

audits.other_findings: Proformas or checklists recommended to improve pTNM staging documentation.
audits.citation: Pradhan AP, Menon S, Rekhi B, Deodhar K. An Audit of 204 Histopathology Reports Over Three Years of Carcinoma of Cervix: Experience from a Tertiary Referral Centre. Asian Pac J Cancer Prev. 2015;16(14):5643-5645. doi:10.7314/apjcp.2015.16.14.5643. PMID: 26320429.

audits.title: Assessment of Reporting Completeness in Prostate Core Biopsies: A Four-Year Audit From a Tertiary Care Centre (2021-2024).
audits.standard: CAP Prostate Cancer Protocol (2023), WHO 2022 classification and ISUP Gleason grading guidance
audits.setting: Histopathology Department, Sultan Qaboos University Hospital, tertiary care, Muscat

cycle1.result: Gleason parameters complete in 100%; tumour type 94%; WHO/ISUP Grade Group 95%; perineural invasion 97%; tumour percentage per core 92%; gross description complete in all.

audits.citation: Qureshi A, Al Sulaimani A, Qureshi H, Al Riyami M. Assessment of Reporting Completeness in Prostate Core Biopsies: A Four-Year Audit From a Tertiary Care Centre (2021-2024). Cureus. 2026;18(3):e104516. doi:10.7759/cureus.104516. PMID: 41930051.

audits.title: Evidence of effectiveness of clinical audit in improving histopathology reporting standards of mastectomy specimens.
audits.standard: Agreed written departmental guidelines with six essential pieces of information in mastectomy reports
audits.setting: Department of Pathology, University of Wales College of Medicine, Cardiff

cycle1.result: 0 of 10 reports included all six mandatory items.

audits.intervention: Written reporting guidelines (audited 1992 and 1994), then a reporting proforma introduced before 1996.

cycle2.result: All 10 reports contained all mandatory information.

audits.other_findings: After written guidelines 4 of 10 reports were complete in 1992, falling to 1 of 10 in 1994, showing standards decline without continued monitoring.
audits.citation: Appleton MA, Douglas-Jones AG, Morgan JM. Evidence of effectiveness of clinical audit in improving histopathology reporting standards of mastectomy specimens. J Clin Pathol. 1998;51(1):30-33. doi:10.1136/jcp.51.1.30. PMID: 9577368.

audits.title: An Audit of Narrative Reports Compared to Structured Pathology Reporting for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
audits.standard: Australian structured pathology reporting guidelines for non-melanoma skin cancer (2023)
audits.setting: University hospital multidisciplinary team (Pathology Queensland, Sunshine Coast)

cycle1.result: Macroscopic criteria reported in 95%-100%; most microscopic criteria 94%-100%; lymphovascular invasion 80%, depth of invasion 33%, satellitosis/in-transit metastasis 0%.

audits.other_findings: 156 cSCC cases were referred to MDT, 87 met inclusion criteria; authors suggest structured reports may improve completeness.
audits.citation: Dettrick A, Tayyab A, Kuballa A, Donkin R, Lambie D. An Audit of Narrative Reports Compared to Structured Pathology Reporting for Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma. Australas J Dermatol. 2025;66(4):204-209. doi:10.1111/ajd.14486. PMID: 40213877.
